intent: The veil drawn over the page behind a drawer's panel, fading as the panel is swiped away.
typical_uses: A visible veil behind a drawer whose `modal` is `false` or `'trap-focus'`, where DrawerContent draws none, placed inside a DrawerPortal

dont_use_when.situation: The backdrop of an ordinary modal drawer

instead.note: DrawerContent renders this backdrop itself while the root's `modal` is `true`.

invariants.text: DrawerBackdrop is a layer covering the whole viewport with the role `presentation`, a light var(--overlay-panel) tint and, where the browser supports `backdrop-filter`, a blur of var(--overlay-panel-blur) over what is behind it.

Its opacity falls as the panel is swiped toward its edge, never below 0.5 while the drawer is open and has `snapPoints`, when DrawerContent draws it (only that backdrop is stamped `data-snap-points`); it fades in over 450ms and out over at most 400ms, which a faster dismiss swipe shortens.
The primitive renders it only for a drawer that is not nested inside another one, unless `forceRender` is set.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the backdrop's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the backdrop's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, transitionStatus). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through drawer.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A veil behind a drawer that traps focus without locking page scroll

bad.title: A second backdrop added to a modal drawer
bad.why: DrawerContent already draws a backdrop while `modal` is `true`, so this stacks a second tint and blur over the page.
